title: Static and instance methods
context: How do static methods differ from instance methods?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java basics questions (1 of 3)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: A static method belongs to the class. You call it as `ClassName.method()` and it has no `this`, so it cannot read instance fields directly. It is resolved at compile time, so it cannot be overridden, only hidden. An instance method belongs to an object, has access to `this`, and is dispatched at run time, so subclasses can override it. Use static for helpers that need no object state.

points.title: No this in static methods
points.why: A static method has no object, so it cannot touch instance state.

points.title: Overriding does not apply
points.why: Static methods are hidden, not overridden, so the method called depends on the declared type.
